title: Lee's view of Lester's induction and the army's posting of black soldiers
summary: Lee thinks Lester should have gone to a band like Great Lakes, recalls him jumping the wall at Fort MacArthur, and says black soldiers were shipped south.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: if I had not been rejected, I was on my way to Great Lakes. But when I was to be examined, I had requested that that was the band I wanted to go in, because that was Snooky Young, and there was Gerald Wilson, and there was Willie Smith, you know, and Jimmy the trumpet player ... good trumpet player, was in the ...

Yeah, Jimmy Nottingham was in the Great Lakes band, Dudley Brooks was in the Great Lakes band, and out here at the Santa Anna air base, all the studio musicians were at Santa Anna air base, because I used to go out there and play with them all the time. But I think that he was railroaded because, maybe part of it was his fault, I don't know -- because I was working at the Downbeat here, and I took him downtown, down on 8th Street to be inducted, and he was inducted and went to Fort MacArthur, but that night he was sitting right in the front row when I opened up and started playing.

I said, 'What are you doing here?' And he said, 'I jumped the wall.' You know, and so he came over the wall and I took him back, and he went back over the wall and got back in camp, but it's a thing that he could not adjust to, you know? And I think that ... it's all past now, but I do think that it was unfair because he was a musician, and at the time, the caliber of musician that you were, then you did have a chance not to be -- but they put him in just the army,

just like any other buck private.
Sure, maybe I could have adjusted to it in all probability, but you're talking about a different type of person, you know? Joe Jones couldn't adjust to it, either. They had him in, you know, and he was a raving maniac, also. But most of the musicians I know did not have to carry that -- they didn't have to hack that, you know. But I think you're dealing with personalities when you get in to that, because it was his misfortune to probably get on the wrong track with whomever the officer was here at Fort MacArthur. And that's why they shipped him south.
But I will say this -- I never did understand this about the army. Most of the black guys, if they were from the East or of California, they always shipped them south. They did it -- to a man. They always shipped them south. And all the southern boys, they shipped them to the West Coast or the East Coast. I'm speaking of black soldiers. When they sould induct them in Georgia or Mississippi, they would ship them to California; they'd be stationed in California, in Illinois, or in New York or Jersey.
But the guys from Jersey or New York and California and like that, they would ship them to Mississippi and Georgia; you know, it was like they were trying to prove something. You know. So that's about all I know about the story about Lester.
